issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters (returns int), but the solution implements getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests). This signature mismatch is structural: students following the specification or tests expecting a no-argument method will be unable to use the solution's version without changing the method signature or tests.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the solution with the problem/UML by providing a no-argument method: change the solution to implement public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() that returns numberOfInscribedStudents + numberOfGuestStudents. If a variant that excludes guests is desired, add an overloaded method (e.g. getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests)) in addition to the required no-arg method, so the UML/tests remain satisfied.

issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a method getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters (returning the total number of students). The solution implementation uses getTotalNumberOfStudents(boolean includeGuests) (a different signature that requires a boolean). This mismatch between the expected no-arg method and the solution's boolean-parameter method can confuse students mapping the requirement to the reference implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the solution match the problem statement: implement getTotalNumberOfStudents() with no parameters (returning inscribed + guest students). Optionally, keep the boolean overload for additional behavior but ensure the no-arg signature exists and delegates to the param version (e.g., add public int getTotalNumberOfStudents() { return getTotalNumberOfStudents(true); }). Alternatively, update the problem statement and UML to document the boolean parameter if that was the intended design.
